objects.summary: P2 review finds Q8 marked complete while Q9 still carries pre-Q8 BLOCKED text and stale placeholder references; because autopilot selects only READY tasks, Astra review could silently fail to launch.
Builder/Owner reply confirms the Q9 inconsistency was already corrected: references updated, Q9 moved READY then IN_PROGRESS, and Astra was launched at 00:58Z. No further action required.
P2 review finds a2_team_status.py ignores git fetch/read failures; stale or absent refs can be interpreted as no READY work and marker state can be overwritten, turning uncertainty into false idle.
P2 review finds a2_publish_block.py treats every backticked 64-hex value anywhere in a comment as a declared publication checksum, so documentary SHA references can create false rejection.
P2 review finds the team-status branch allowlist already omits active/future task branches such as Q15/Q23; wake logic can miss new work and incorrectly conclude no useful event arrived.

P2 review finds the checksum parser still accepts blocks when hash appears anywhere rather than only among explicitly declared publication checksums; declaration semantics must be distinct from documentary references.
P1 review finds watchdog ignores a raw authentic Owner STOP because STOP lacks an A2-TEAM header, so old waits can continue to wake/ping an explicitly stopped team.
P1 review finds any later comment by the target is treated as closing a wait even if unrelated; waits need causal IDs/references rather than mere later activity.
P2 review finds watchdog emits no durable dedupe state for reminders; the same expired wait or silence alert can be reissued every scheduled run, creating an expensive wake loop.

cross_object_findings.finding: Inline reviews identified queue-state, branch-monitoring and watchdog defects capable of stopping or misrouting automation despite valid work existing. These reviews changed execution behavior rather than style.
Fetch/read failures must terminate a coordination decision as UNKNOWN/BLOCK; converting stale or failed reads into no-work/idle can silently halt progress.
Publication integrity requires explicit binding between a declared checksum and its block; merely finding the same hash elsewhere in text is insufficient.
Without STOP precedence, causal closure IDs and durable reminder dedupe, a watchdog can both miss unfinished waits and amplify noise with repeated wake/alert actions.
